purpose: Thirteenth expanded public source layer focused on enzyme-aware strategic disconnections for ketoreductase chiral alcohol formation, transaminase/imine-reductase chiral amines, site-selective enzymatic halogenation, P450 and oxygenase late-stage C-H oxidation, glycosyltransferase-mediated glycodiversification, Baeyer-Villiger monooxygenase oxygen insertion, aldolase/transketolase C-C bond formation, and terpene cyclase or PKS/NRPS biosynthetic assembly-line boundaries.

promotion_requirements: explicit substrate, product, enzyme class, stereochemical outcome, and cofactor or donor metadata before proposal promotion
separate ketoreductase, transaminase, imine-reductase, halogenase, P450, glycosyltransferase, BVMO, aldolase, transketolase, terpene-cyclase, PKS, and NRPS policy
route-specific enzyme scope, cofactor recycling, donor/acceptor identity, site selectivity, stereochemical model, cascade order, and biosynthetic-module review
biological-mode, antimicrobial, toxin, metabolic-engineering, expression-host, environmental, or process-safety review where relevant
safety_scope: records intentionally avoid quantities, operational procedures, expression protocols, and synthesis conditions
enzyme records are precedent-backed strategic priors only and must not auto-close routes as stock or executable wet-lab recipes

families.name: Ketoreductase and alcohol-dehydrogenase chiral alcohol route anchors
families.strategic_principle: Separate prochiral ketone synthesis, enzyme stereopreference, cofactor recycling, and product alcohol configuration. A chiral alcohol made by KRED/ADH logic is not an ordinary hydride reduction.

families.name: Transaminase, imine-reductase, and reductive-aminase chiral amine route anchors
families.strategic_principle: Separate carbonyl/imine precursor design, amine donor or partner, enzyme family, and amine stereochemistry. The enzyme class determines whether the strategic move is transamination, imine reduction, or direct reductive amination.

families.name: Flavin-dependent, alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent, and late-stage enzymatic halogenation
families.strategic_principle: Separate scaffold synthesis from enzyme-controlled halogen placement, halide identity, cofactor system, and biosynthetic context. Halogenase selectivity is route-defining metadata, not a generic aryl halide decoration.

families.name: P450, peroxygenase, and oxygenase late-stage C-H oxidation route anchors
families.strategic_principle: Separate advanced scaffold synthesis from site-selective enzymatic oxidation, oxygenase identity, redox partner, and metabolite or analogue objective. Enzymatic C-H oxidation can be the strategic route handle.

families.name: Glycosyltransferase donor-acceptor strategy and glycodiversification boundaries
families.strategic_principle: Separate aglycone assembly, sugar-nucleotide donor preparation, glycosyltransferase acceptor scope, and attachment site. Sugar identity and donor/acceptor pairing are strategic route fields.

families.name: Baeyer-Villiger monooxygenase lactone, ester, and cascade oxygen-insertion anchors
families.strategic_principle: Separate ketone or cyclic ketone precursor design from enzyme-controlled oxygen insertion, migratory aptitude, cofactor recycling, and lactone/ester regiochemistry.

families.name: Aldolase, transketolase, and enzyme-mediated asymmetric C-C bond formation
families.strategic_principle: Separate carbonyl partners, donor identity, enzyme family, and stereochemical array. Enzyme-catalyzed C-C formation can replace a chemical aldol or umpolung step when substrate scope is explicit.

families.name: Terpene cyclase, PKS, and NRPS biosynthetic assembly-line boundaries
families.strategic_principle: Separate linear isoprenoid, acyl-chain, or peptide assembly from enzyme-programmed cyclization, module order, tailoring domains, and pathway-engineering feasibility. Biosynthetic modules are source records, not stock materials.

anchors.name: KRED/ADH chiral alcohol anchor with reviewed ketone substrate, stereopreference, and cofactor policy
TA/IRED/RedAm chiral amine anchor with reviewed carbonyl or imine precursor and enzyme family
Halogenase anchor with reviewed substrate class, halide identity, and enzyme-controlled site selectivity
P450 or oxygenase late-stage oxidation anchor with reviewed oxidation site and redox system
Glycosyltransferase anchor with reviewed aglycone acceptor, sugar donor, and attachment site
BVMO oxygen-insertion anchor with reviewed ketone precursor, regiochemistry, and cofactor policy
Aldolase/transketolase C-C bond anchor with reviewed donor, acceptor, and stereochemical array
Terpene cyclase or PKS/NRPS assembly-line anchor with reviewed precursor, module order, and tailoring logic

disconnections.name: Chiral alcohol to prochiral ketone plus KRED/ADH stereopreference and cofactor policy

forward_logic: synthesize or identify the corresponding prochiral ketone
track KRED or ADH stereopreference and cofactor recycling as route metadata
carry product configuration into route ranking
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward routes that expose enzyme stereopreference and cofactor policy instead of treating the step as a generic hydride reduction.

evidence.citation: Ketoreductase update review covers asymmetric synthesis of chiral secondary alcohol pharmaceutical and bioactive intermediates.
Enzymatic asymmetric synthesis review covers ADH/KRED reductions as a broadly useful stereoselective strategy.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit ketone precursor, enzyme stereopreference, product configuration, and cofactor policy

disconnections.name: KRED kinetic or dynamic kinetic resolution to racemate plus enzyme selectivity and racemization policy

forward_logic: separate racemate or epimerizable substrate preparation from enzymatic resolution
track whether selectivity is KR, DKR, or deracemization-like
require explicit mass-balance and stereochemical interpretation before promotion
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use this entry only when the strategic value is stereochemical resolution or DKR, not simple carbonyl reduction.

risks: yield ceiling for ordinary kinetic resolution

evidence.citation: KRED kinetic and dynamic kinetic resolution review covers biomanufacturing of chiral chemicals with multiple stereocenters.
Industrial enzymatic synthesis review discusses KREDs as major methods for making chiral alcohols.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit KR/DKR role, stereochemical accounting, and enzyme selectivity

disconnections.name: Chiral primary amine to ketone or aldehyde plus transaminase donor/equilibrium policy

break_bonds: C-N bond from carbonyl amination boundary
forward_logic: disconnect the amine to the corresponding ketone or aldehyde precursor
track amine donor, equilibrium strategy, and transaminase enantiopreference
separate enzyme selection from ordinary reductive amination templates
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward transaminase routes when donor/equilibrium handling and enzyme stereopreference are explicit.

evidence.citation: Transaminase review discusses chiral primary amine synthesis by amine transaminases.
Transaminase industrial biocatalysis review covers discovery, engineering, and chiral amine applications.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit carbonyl precursor, amine donor, equilibrium strategy, and enzyme enantiopreference

disconnections.name: Secondary or tertiary chiral amine to imine/carbonyl plus IRED or RedAm reduction policy

forward_logic: separate carbonyl and amine partners from enzymatic imine formation/reduction
track whether the enzyme is an imine reductase, reductive aminase, amine dehydrogenase, or related scaffold
carry NAD(P)H and stereochemical metadata into route ranking
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use IRED/RedAm entries when enzyme family determines whether imine formation and reduction are both plausible.

evidence.citation: IRED and reductive-aminase review discusses reductive aminations from milligram to ton scale.
NAD(P)H-dependent dehydrogenase review covers imine reductases and related asymmetric reductive amination biocatalysts.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit imine/carbonyl precursor, amine partner, enzyme class, cofactor, and stereochemical outcome

disconnections.name: Aryl halide product to unhalogenated scaffold plus flavin-dependent halogenase site-selectivity policy

forward_logic: disconnect to the unhalogenated aromatic substrate
track halogenase family, halide identity, and position selectivity
flag enzyme records for substrate-scope and cofactor review
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward enzymatic halogenation only when the target halogen position matches known or reviewed enzyme selectivity.

evidence.citation: Flavin-dependent halogenase review discusses catalyst-controlled halogenation, mutagenesis, and biocatalysis applications.
Flavin-dependent biocatalyst review covers halogenase-mediated halogenation and synthetic selectivity.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit unhalogenated precursor, halogenase family, halide identity, and site selectivity

disconnections.name: Aliphatic or noncanonical halogenated product to substrate plus alpha-ketoglutarate halogenase policy

forward_logic: separate substrate scaffold from enzyme-catalyzed halogen placement
track halogenating-enzyme family and biosynthetic context
avoid promoting halogenated targets without explicit enzyme precedent
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use this entry for biosynthetic halogenation critique when halogen placement is enzyme-defined and not reproduced by generic halogenation templates.

risks: halogenated bioactive compound safety review required

evidence.citation: Halogenating-enzyme review covers flavin-dependent and alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent halogenases and biotechnological applications.
Recent drug-synthesis biocatalysis review includes halogenation among API-relevant late-stage biocatalytic developments.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit enzyme family, substrate class, halogen placement, and biosynthetic context

disconnections.name: Hydroxylated analogue to parent scaffold plus P450 late-stage oxidation policy

break_bonds: C-H to C-OH late-stage oxidation boundary
forward_logic: disconnect to the parent scaffold or metabolite precursor
track P450/oxygenase identity, oxidation site, and redox support
rank routes only when site selectivity is supported by evidence
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward oxygenase routes when a late-stage oxidation replaces lengthy de novo oxygenated-scaffold synthesis with explicit site-selectivity evidence.

evidence.citation: P450 late-stage functionalization review discusses use of P450 enzymes in drug discovery.
Enzymatic late-stage modification review covers oxygenases including P450s for early and late-stage functionalization.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit parent scaffold, oxidation site, enzyme identity, and redox support

disconnections.name: Metabolite or hydroxylated reference standard to parent drug plus oxygenating-biocatalyst policy

forward_logic: separate parent-drug scaffold access from biocatalytic metabolite generation
track whether route objective is isolation, analogue generation, or reference-standard synthesis
flag bioactive metabolite records for toxicology and analytical validation
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use oxygenase metabolite entries for route critique when the product is valuable because it matches a biologically relevant oxidation pattern.

evidence.citation: Oxygenating-biocatalyst review discusses hydroxyl functionalization for drug discovery and development.
Biocatalysis drug-synthesis review includes late-stage functionalization and oxyfunctionalization for APIs.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit parent scaffold, metabolite site, oxygenase class, and validation objective

disconnections.name: Natural-product glycoside to aglycone acceptor plus sugar-nucleotide donor and GT scope

target_classes: plant or microbial glycosylated small molecules

forward_logic: disconnect the glycoside into aglycone acceptor and sugar donor roles
track glycosyltransferase family, donor identity, and acceptor-site scope
separate enzymatic donor/acceptor policy from ordinary chemical glycosylation
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward glycosyltransferase routes when donor identity, acceptor site, and enzyme scope are explicit.

evidence.citation: Natural-product sugar biosynthesis review covers sugar donors, glycosyltransferases, and glycodiversification.
Plant natural-product glycosyltransferase review covers mining, engineering, and biosynthetic applications.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit aglycone, sugar donor, attachment site, and transferase scope

disconnections.name: Glycodiversified analogue to sugar-activation module plus promiscuous GT policy

forward_logic: separate aglycone construction from sugar biosynthesis or sugar-nucleotide activation
track donor engineering, GT promiscuity, and analogue-library intent
flag glycodiversification entries for biological-mode and manufacturing review
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use glycodiversification entries when analogue value depends on sugar exchange rather than aglycone rebuilding.

evidence.citation: Enzyme-engineering glycodiversification review highlights natural-product glycosyltransferases and donor modules.
Small-molecule glycosyltransferase-mediated glycodiversification review covers enzymatic glycodiversification advances.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit sugar-activation module, GT promiscuity, and library provenance

disconnections.name: Lactone or ester to ketone precursor plus BVMO oxygen-insertion and regiochemistry policy

forward_logic: disconnect lactone or ester product to the corresponding ketone precursor
track BVMO class, migratory aptitude, cofactor recycling, and product regiochemistry
avoid generic peracid BV templates when enzymatic selectivity is the strategic reason
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward BVMO routes when ketone precursor access and enzyme-controlled oxygen insertion explain product selectivity.

evidence.citation: BVMO review describes discovery, application, and protein engineering for organic synthesis.
BVMO application review covers biocatalytic processes and high-value compound synthesis.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit ketone precursor, BVMO identity, cofactor policy, and lactone/ester regiochemistry

disconnections.name: Biocatalytic lactone/lactam product to oxidation cascade plus BVMO or hydrolase pathway policy

forward_logic: separate upstream alcohol/alkane/ketone generation from lactone or lactam-forming enzyme step
track cascade order and cofactor compatibility
require explicit endpoint identity before route scoring
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use this entry when the strategic route object is an enzyme cascade leading to lactone or lactam, not a single named oxidation.

evidence.citation: Biocatalytic lactone/lactam synthesis review discusses BVMO and related enzymatic alternatives.
In vitro redox-cascade study demonstrates an ADH/enoate-reductase/BVMO enzymatic toolbox for lactone-forming cascades.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit cascade order, endpoint identity, and cofactor compatibility

disconnections.name: Beta-hydroxy carbonyl or polyhydroxy fragment to aldehyde/ketone partners plus aldolase stereocontrol

forward_logic: disconnect to carbonyl donor and acceptor roles
track aldolase class, donor identity, and stereochemical array
compare enzymatic aldol logic against chemical aldol/crotylation alternatives
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward aldolase routes when the enzyme explains simultaneous C-C bond formation and stereochemical array control.

evidence.citation: Aldolase engineering review discusses aldolases as C-C bond-forming biocatalysts.
Enzymatic asymmetric synthesis review includes C-C bond formation by nucleophilic carbon addition.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: high for explicit donor/acceptor pair, aldolase class, and stereochemical array

disconnections.name: Ketol or dihydroxy fragment to aldehyde acceptor plus transketolase donor-transfer policy

forward_logic: disconnect product to aldehyde acceptor and ketol donor roles
track ThDP-dependent transketolase class and donor thermodynamics
flag routes where charged or highly polar substrate recognition dominates feasibility
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use transketolase entries when C2 donor transfer and enzyme active-site recognition are strategic feasibility drivers.

evidence.citation: Transketolase study discusses asymmetric C-C bond formation of polar compounds and substrate binding.
Biocatalytic C-C bond formation review includes transketolase and related C1-resource utilization enzymes.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit donor, aldehyde acceptor, ThDP enzyme class, and thermodynamic policy

disconnections.name: Terpene skeleton to linear prenyl precursor plus cyclase-controlled cation cascade policy

forward_logic: separate linear isoprenoid precursor generation from cyclase-controlled ring construction
track terpene synthase class, carbocation cascade, and product selectivity
avoid flattening terpene skeletons into generic cationic cyclization templates
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Reward terpene-cyclase routes when ring topology is best explained by enzyme-templated cation cascade logic.

evidence.citation: Terpenoid cyclase review covers structural and chemical biology of terpene cyclase catalysis and engineering.
Non-canonical terpene synthase review discusses structure, enzymology, and opportunities for terpene biosynthesis.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit linear precursor, terpene cyclase class, and cyclization topology

disconnections.name: PKS/NRPS-derived product to starter/extender or amino-acid units plus module/domain policy

forward_logic: separate chemical synthesis of building blocks from biosynthetic module logic
track PKS/NRPS domain order, carrier-protein tethering, and tailoring enzymes
treat pathway engineering as a source-backed strategy rather than ordinary fragment coupling
suggested_precursor_roles: extender unit or amino-acid building block
retrosynthetic_move.planner_hint: Use PKS/NRPS entries for route critique when module order and biosynthetic feasibility dominate over normal retrosynthetic bond disconnections.

evidence.citation: PKS/NRPS engineering review discusses engineering substrate specificity, activity, and protein interactions of biosynthetic machinery.
Polyketide chemoenzymatic synthesis review covers PKS assembly-line studies and natural-product derivatives.

use_policy.rerank_bonus: moderate for explicit module order, building-block logic, carrier-protein constraints, and tailoring domains

source_notes.summary: The v14 expansion promotes the biocatalytic strategic-source backlog into enzyme-aware source records for KRED/ADH, TA/IRED/RedAm, halogenase, P450/oxygenase, glycosyltransferase, BVMO, aldolase/transketolase, terpene cyclase, and PKS/NRPS route logic.

Biocatalytic records are advisory and evidence-gated. Promotion to proposal generation requires explicit substrate scope, enzyme identity, stereochemical or site-selectivity support, cofactor/donor handling, pathway context, and biological/process safety review.
